amino acid residues in IS6 and IISS6 of the sodium channel α subunit play critical roles in voltage-dependent gating and drug block.
amino acid residues in IS6 and I IS6 of the Na channel α subunit are critical to voltage-dependent activation and inactivation and to the local anesthetic block of the channel.

amino acid residues in transmembrane segments (TM) IS6 and IIs6 of the rat Nav1.2 α subunit are critical for the gating properties and block of the Na+ channel by local anesthetics and neuroprotective drugs.

the molecular mechanisms underlying the voltage dependence of Na+ channel activation, inactivation, and drug block.
the role of specific amino acid residues in the transmembrane segments of voltage-gated Na+ channels.

the role of amino acid residues in the S6 transmembrane segments of the sodium channel α subunit in the voltage-dependent gating of sodium channels, and with the interaction between these residues and the inactivated-state binding site for local anesthetic and neuroprotective drug compounds.

IS6 and I IS6 are involved in voltage sensing, inactivation gating, and drug block of the Na+ channel α subunit.
the amino acid residues of IS6 and IS6 are involved in the voltage sensing and the gating of the channel.
the IS6 and I IS6 transmembrane segments of the Na+ channel α subunit have a major role in the voltage dependence and gating of the Na+ channels, but the exact mechanism is not clear.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the IS6 and I IS6 segments of the Na+ channel α subunit play a major role in determining the voltage dependence of channel activation, inactivation from closed and open states, inactivation from open states, and local anesthetic block of the inactivated state.

the amino acids in segments IS6 and IIIS6 play a role in the voltage-dependent activation and inactivation gating of the Na+ channel α subunit.
